pages.text: When heat beats the coolers, the cells warm toward -180C. Fix the cooling in time and they cool back down and sound the all clear.

pages.title: Warning Time
pages.text: From the first chirp to the quench:$(li)about 15 min outside below 0C$(li)about 5 min in a 20C room$(li)90 s with a heat source against the hull: lava, fire, a heater, a hot radiator or a running reactor

pages.title: What You Hear
pages.text: In order:$(li)A chirp every 10 s$(li)A steady ping as time runs short$(li)A rising whine for the last 25 s$(br2)The whine stops if it recovers.

pages.title: Quench
pages.text: A bang, steam from the vent, and the charge is gone. Nothing else is damaged.$(br2)The cells stay scorched and hold no charge until they are cold again. The coolers draw grid power to get there.

pages.title: Taking It Down
pages.text: Breaking any part while it holds charge quenches it at once, with no warning. Explosions and pistons count too.$(br2)Empty, it comes apart quietly.
